sections.html:
Two offices handle your tax life, and they do different jobs. The appraiser decides what the house is worth and who gets an exemption. The collector mails the bill, takes payment and distributes the revenue. If a name, address or assessed value is wrong on the roll, go to the appraiser, not the collector.

The appraiser's main office is at 312 Oak Street in Palatka, with a mailing box at PO Box 1920, Palatka, FL 32178. Satellite offices in Crescent City (Mondays and Wednesdays) and Interlachen (Tuesdays and Thursdays) keep set days. The exemption department's number is (386) 329-0286. Property tax pages for the collector are at putnamtax.com, and tax certificate sales run through an online bidding site.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, tangible personal property, roll corrections.
  • Tax Collector: bills, discounts, installments, delinquent taxes and certificates.
  • Clerk of the Court: tax deed sales and recorded deeds.

One Putnam bill can combine lines from the county, a fire district, the school board, two water management districts and one of five municipalities. The collector's website gives a phone number for each, so you can ask the right office about its rate.

The roster: the county, the Fire MSTU District, the Putnam County School Board, the St. Johns River Water Management District, the Suwannee Water Management District, the City of Palatka, the City of Crescent City, and the Towns of Interlachen, Pomona Park and Welaka. A parcel inside a city pays that city's levy on top of the county's.

Non-ad valorem charges ride beside the tax lines. The county added a solid waste assessment on residential units, divided among landfill improvements, garbage collection and recycling. Commissioners have also approved 28 separate MSBU projects for road maintenance or paving, which charge only the parcels that benefit. The Hastings Drainage District has its own assessment. Homestead doesn't reduce any of these, and a buyer will see them on the bill.

Assessments are pegged to January 1 and collection typically begins November 1. Pay the gross figure by March 31 or the real estate account is delinquent from April 1.

Early payment discounts on current real estate taxes
Payment monthDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone, gross amount due

Owners with an estimated bill above $100 can use a quarterly installment plan. Your application must be in the office by April 30 ahead of the first payment year. Payments come due June 30 (6% discount), September 30 (4.5%), December 31 (3%) and March 31 (no discount). Miss the June payment and the account drops out of the plan until the next year, when you apply again. The first two payments are based on the prior year's taxes and the last two on the new roll.

Delinquent parcels are advertised in a local newspaper three weeks running, and a certificate sale is held online by June 1. A certificate is a lien. It doesn't hand over the house.

Bidding opens at 18% and falls in quarter percent steps, and the lowest bidder gets the certificate. Owners who redeem afterward can owe interest of up to 18% a year, depending on the winning bid rate. After delinquency the office accepts cashier's check, certified check, cash or money order, and the amount due is set by the day it receives your payment.

  • If taxes stay unpaid two years from April 1, the certificate holder can usually file a tax deed application.
  • Applications run through RealTDA, and the county keeps a Lands Available for Taxes list of parcels that drew no bidder.
  • Paying the taxes cancels the lien, but every payment after delinquency must be in certified funds.

Selling a house that carries a certificate? Get a redemption quote from the collector and give it to the closing agent early. Interest keeps accruing until the lien is cleared.

Homestead removes the first $25,000 of value from every ad valorem levy. It leaves special assessments alone. The Palatka office takes applications all year, and the satellite offices help during the first two months of the year.

Exemption applications are due March 1, counted from the year after you buy. Later filers also have to complete an Extenuating Circumstances form. On the assessment date you need title in your name, Florida permanent residency and the house serving as your primary home. Proof includes a Florida driver license or ID with the home address, and a Florida vehicle registration. Trust-owned homes get a closer review.

  • Low income senior exemption: a county ordinance adds $25,000 against the county general millage for homeowners 65 and over under the income limit. Ask the office for the current limit.
  • Super Senior exemption: for 25-year residents with a just value under $250,000, it exempts the whole assessed value where a taxing authority has enacted it. Putnam County, Palatka, Crescent City, Interlachen, Pomona Park and Welaka have.
  • Deployed service member, total and permanent disability and first responder exemptions, each with its own proof requirements.

An approved exemption renews by itself, but you must report a change in use or status right away.

sections.h2: How a sale changes the next bill
sections.html:
The buyer's first roll starts at just value, and any exemption you held stays behind. Florida treats a sale, foreclosure or title transfer as a change of ownership. Spouses and certain transfers at death are exceptions.

A house one family has held for years may carry a bill that looks small next to what the new owner sees on the first full roll. The assessment cap, set at 2.7% on the state's 2026 chart, applies only while the same owner keeps the homestead. If you're moving within Florida, the portability form can carry up to $500,000 of your accrued benefit to the new homestead, filed with the exemption application by March 1.

Deed stamps cost $0.70 per $100 of price and are paid through the Clerk when the deed records. The contract may shift the cost to one party, but anyone named on the deed remains liable.

Before you list, confirm three things: the current bill is paid or will be settled at closing, no tax certificate is outstanding, and the exemption record matches how you use the house. Renting the house out, or moving away, ends homestead.

Both offices are in Palatka and the roll is public. Print the parcel record and the bill and hand both to the closing agent. Ask whether any MSBU road assessment or solid waste charge is unpaid, since those ride on the same bill as the taxes.

Collect this paperwork now, before offers arrive:

  1. The latest tax bill with proof it was paid.
  2. Any exemption approval letters.
  3. Payoff statements for a mortgage, a lien or a certificate.
  4. Notes on assessments that will carry over to the buyer.

With a cash buyer, the same payoff and proration steps happen at closing, just with fewer lender conditions in the way.

faqs.q: How much can I save by paying early?
faqs.a: The discount is 4% for November and drops a point each month through February. March carries none. Bills open for collection November 1.

faqs.q: When do Putnam County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Anything unpaid after March 31 is delinquent the next day and heads for a certificate sale by June 1.
Yes. The quarterly plan needs an application in by April 30 and an estimated bill over $100. Its first three payments carry 6%, 4.5% and 3% discounts.

faqs.q: Where do I file for homestead?
faqs.a: File with the Property Appraiser in Palatka, or at the Crescent City or Interlachen satellite office during the winter filing season. The cutoff is March 1 after you buy.

faqs.q: Can I lose my house over unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Eventually, yes. After two years a certificate holder may seek a tax deed and the house can go to auction. Paying the full amount before the sale keeps it yours.
